episodes.content:
The sky did not exist beneath the Citadel’s belly, only an endless, roaring throat of cold air and calcified mana. 

Sir Silas Vance fell through the darkness, the wind tearing the breath from his throat before it could form a curse. Below him, the shattered core of the Warden Prime tumbled through the gloom, a dying miniature sun spitting jagged violet embers into the abyss. Above, the stone walkway he had stood upon moments ago was nothing more than a jagged scar of broken basalt disappearing into smoke.

His left eye—the unnatural, glass-like orb forced into his skull by the High Council’s flesh-crafters years ago—did not weep. It burned. The corrupted cosmic essence inside it pulsed in sickening sync with the falling core below, radiating a heat so intense it charred the skin around his cheekbone. Visions bled through his optic nerve: geometric sigils written in white fire, planetary arrays shifting like clockwork, and a single, terrifying command burning through the lattice of the Grand Cosmic grid.

*Purge phase: Initiated.*

"Not today," Silas growled through gritted teeth. 

He twisted his body mid-fall, wrapping both gauntleted hands around the leather-bound hilt of his heavy broadsword. The ancient runes etched along the blade flared with a faint, stubborn gold—the dying light of a Solar Knight’s oath. With a roar that split his dry throat, he drove the point into the passing flank of a massive structural support beam—a giant rib of black steel that held the Citadel’s underbelly above the deep floor.

Metal screamed on metal. A torrent of blinding white sparks sprayed across his face plate as the sword’s edge bit into the alloy, carving a glowing trench down the beam. The jerk nearly ripped Silas’s shoulders from their sockets. Heavy plate armor groaned under the sudden deceleration; his boots slammed against the vertical metal face, skidding wildly before his downward momentum snapped to a violent halt.

He hung there, twenty feet above a yawning platform of forgotten stone, suspended by steel and sheer muscle.

Silas exhaled a shuddering breath, the air bursting from his nose in red-tinged frost. The atmospheric pressure down here was unnatural, dense enough to make his lungs feel as though they were filled with wet sand. He dragged himself upward, wedging his boot into a seam in the support structure, and wrenched his broadsword free from the groaning metal. He dropped to the stone floor below, rolling hard onto his left shoulder to absorb the impact.

The stone beneath him did not feel like natural rock. It hummed. Deep beneath his boots, a massive, subterranean pulse rattled through the soles of his greaves—a slow, rhythmic *thump-thump* like the heartbeat of an imprisoned god.

"Lyra," he muttered, reaching for the brass communication stone strapped to his gorget. He tapped the runic housing. Nothing but the harsh, static hiss of dead cosmic mana filled his ear. "Damn it."

***

Three hundred feet above, in the claustrophobic corridor outside the blasted containment doors, Lyra Thorne did not need a communication stone to know the world was unraveling.

The floor beneath her boots tilted at a five-degree angle. She crouched low, her palm pressed flat against the floorboards. To an ordinary rogue, the world was merely stone and iron, but to Lyra’s eyes, the ambient ley lines of the Citadel were visible as shimmering threads of radiant indigo and sickly lime green. Right now, those threads were snapping one by one, releasing bursts of pressurized magic that smelled faintly of burnt cinnamon and ozone.

"Cornered little fox," a voice echoed through the lingering smoke.

Heavy, deliberate footsteps crunched over the shattered glass and marble. Three figures emerged from the haze, clad in the pristine, obsidian-and-gold plate of the High Council Inquisitors. Their tall, angular helmets bore no eye-slits; instead, smooth visors of polished starlight stone reflected the dying ambient light of the corridor. Each carried a curved arc-blade, the weapons humming with an agonizingly sharp, high-pitched resonance that made Lyra’s teeth ache.

The lead Inquisitor lowered his blade, the tip hovering inches from her chest. "The knight has taken his secrets to the floor of the Uncreated. You will not join him. The Council requires your eyes, scholar. They wish to harvest what you have seen."

Lyra’s fingers tightened around the hilts of her dual runic daggers. Her heart hammered against her ribs, but her mind remained cold, calculating, dissecting the room.

"You're standing on a structural shear line, bright-eyes," Lyra spat, a sharp, dangerous smile cutting through the grime on her face. "Didn't they teach you basic spatial harmonics in the Academy?"

The lead Inquisitor didn't flinch. "Seize her."

Before the two flanking guards could step forward, Lyra struck. She didn't plunge her daggers into their armor; instead, she slammed both runic blades violently into the floor directly at her feet. 

The ancient runes carved into her daggers flared brilliant crimson. She tapped into the localized ley line, violently diverting the flux of raw, unstable celestial mana straight into the sub-floor's structural anchors. 

The air pressure plummeted instantly, popping the ears of every man in the room. 

A violent white shockwave exploded from the point of impact. The floor gave way with the sound of a shattering mountain. The two flanking Inquisitors screamed as the basalt deck collapsed beneath them, plunging them into the dark, churning abyss below. The lead Inquisitor lunged forward to grab Lyra’s tunic, but she was already airborne, kicking off his chest plate with enough force to push herself backward into the newly opened ventilation flux behind her.

"Silas!" she shouted into the dark as she plummeted into the maintenance chute, sliding down a sheer, slick incline of ancient stone and brass pipes. "If you're dead down there, I swear to the stars I'm turning your armor into scrap!"

***

The air grew progressively colder as Silas limped through the lower vaults. 

His left eye was acting as a compass, pulling him toward the center of the subterranean chamber. The purple glow casting from his socket lit up ancient, forgotten bas-reliefs carved into the monoliths around him: depictions of giant celestial beings bound in chains of sun-metal, their eyes weeping streams of liquid mana into a central furnace.

"The Purge Catalyst," Silas rasped, touching his burning eyelid. "They didn't give me this eye to kill me. They gave it to me so I'd carry the key straight to the engine."

He reached the center of the vault. 

It was a cavernous dome, so vast that the ceiling was lost in shadows. Suspended in the middle of the room, held by six colossal chains of black iron, was an ancient cosmic alignment wheel—a spherical mechanism the size of a fortress, slowly rotating in mid-air without any visible power source. Runes of uncreation, dead for ten thousand years, were beginning to glow with a sickly, violet resurgence around its equator.

A heavy *thud* echoed behind him, followed by a shower of dust and a string of colorful curses.

Silas whirled, broadsword drawn, his good right eye narrowing through the dark.

Lyra tumbled out of a low maintenance conduit, hitting the dust-covered floor in a heap of leather straps, rogue's tools, and flying hair. She scrambled to her feet instantly, her runic daggers drawn, breathing heavily as she backed up against a stone pillar.

"Don't shoot!" she gasped, wiping a streak of black grease from her forehead. "It's just me! Though I almost got sliced in three by an Inquisitor's arc-blade on the way down."

Silas lowered his sword slightly, though his posture remained tense. "You shouldn't have followed me, Lyra."

"And leave you to stumble around in the dark with that cursed glowing eyeball of yours?" She spat onto the stone, catching her breath as she looked around the massive chamber. Her eyes widened, her pupils dilating as she took in the sight of the rotating cosmic wheel. "By the Light... Silas, what is this place?"

"The belly of the beast," Silas said softly, stepping toward the edge of the stone abyss surrounding the floating sphere. "The Warden Prime wasn't a guard. It was an ignition key. When I destroyed it, the explosion triggered the secondary fail-safe. My eye... it's mirroring the signal."

Lyra walked to his side, her gaze darting across the swirling ley lines connecting his left eye to the glowing runes on the gargantuan sphere. She gasped, staggering back a step as the visual input flooded her mind. 

"Silas... the ley lines aren't drawing power from the Citadel," she whispered, her voice trembling with rare, genuine horror. "The Citadel is drawing power from *this*. It's draining the outer sectors—our homes, the slums, the outer worlds. It's pulling every drop of mana out of the lower realms to charge this wheel."

"To what end?" Silas demanded.

"A total reset," Lyra said, turning her terrified eyes to his. "It's an astral purge key. The High Council isn't just trying to quell the rebellion. They're going to wipe the lower sectors off the cosmic map. Erase them completely."

Before Silas could respond, a low, reverberating chime vibrated through the floorboards—a deep, bronze tone that rattled the teeth in his skull. The six massive chains holding the sphere suddenly snapped taut with a deafening metallic screech. 

High above them, at the apex of the cavern, a massive iris door began to grind open. Brilliant, blinding golden light spilled down from the upper Citadel—and down that light came the descending platform of the High Council, flanked by a dozen heavily armed elite vanguards. 

Standing at the front of the platform, clad in robes of woven starlight, was the High Inquisitor himself, his staff hovering in the air before him.

"You are too late, Sir Vance," the High Inquisitor's voice echoed through the chamber, amplified by cosmic magic. "The alignment has begun. Hand over the ocular core, or watch your world burn in the light of uncreation."

Silas raised his runic broadsword, his left eye blazing with an uncontrollable, violent violet flame. 

"Come and take it," Silas growled.

episodes.content:
The air in the deep vault did not merely grow cold; it curdled. Atmospheric pressure plunged with a sudden, ear-popping snap as the massive teeth of the purge wheel ground together, bronze against ancient star-stone. Deep within the iron ribcage of the subterranean machinery, liquid mana hissed through crystal conduits, glowing a bruised, tempestuous violet. 

Sir Silas Vance adjusted his grip on the leather-wrapped hilt of his silver broadsword. Blood, warm and thick, trickled down his cheek from beneath the heavy leather strap covering his left eye socket. Where the drops struck the frost-rimmed floor plates, they did not pool—they hissed, evaporating into tiny wisps of violent, raw cosmic vapor.

"You're bleeding starlight, Silas," Lyra murmured behind him, her voice tight, strained against the sudden oppressive gravity radiating from the vault walls. She pressed her back against his shoulder blades, dual runic daggers drawn, their edge-runes flickering in faint, frantic pulses of pale azure. "The wheel isn't just spinning up. It’s drinking from you."

"I noticed," Silas growled, his jaw tight. "Focus on the ley lines, girl. Tell me there’s a break in this damned clockwork."

"There isn't," she hissed back, her sharp gaze sweeping across the vaulted ceiling where millions of tiny, glowing star-charts carved into the stone were shifting in real-time, realigning with the lower sectors above them. "It’s a closed circuit. The Citadel’s architects built this place to execute a sector by drawing power directly from an unstable core. Your eye is acting as the primary key."

Footsteps echoed down the sweeping obsidian stairwells surrounding the vault perimeter. Heavy, rhythmic, and terrifyingly deliberate. 

High Inquisitor Malakor descended into the blue-hued gloom, clad in polished white-and-gold plate armor that absorbed the shadows rather than reflecting them. Behind him marched six vanguard knights of the High Council, their tower shields etched with nullification runes that hummed at a sickening, low frequency, deadening the ambient magic in the room like damp sand smothered over a fire.

"Sir Silas Vance," Malakor spoke, his voice modulated by the golden visor masking his face, sounding like grinding marble. "Once the proud Shield of the Solar Dawn. Now a rat burrowing beneath the palace he failed to burn."

Silas spat blood onto the stone. The red smear instantly burned blue and dissolved. "Save the sermoning, Malakor. The Council’s getting lazy if they sent an errand boy to do a butcher's job."

"You misunderstand your worth, knight," Malakor said, stopping at the edge of the central walkway, thirty paces away. Beneath them, the abyssal shaft yawned wide, revealing the true scale of the astral purge wheel—a horizontal brass titan half a mile wide, spinning faster with every heartbeat, casting blinding geometric shadows across the abyss. "We did not come to execute you. We came to collect the Council’s property. That eye belongs to the Astral Core of Aethelgard. You stole it during the eclipse."

"It was grafted into him to keep the lower district from collapsing, you bloody tyrant!" Lyra barked, stepping slightly out from behind Silas's shoulder, her blade lowered but her stance coiled. "If you yank that eye out now while the wheel is engaged, the pressure back-feed will crack the bedrock beneath the whole underbelly!"

Malakor did not even turn his visor toward her. "The lower sectors are a cancer upon the Citadel's grace. A crop ready for harvest. Their mana will be reclaimed to fuel the upper spires for another century." He raised a gauntleted hand. The six vanguard knights snapped their sun-forged halberds forward in unison, the tip of each weapon igniting with concentrated solar plasma. "Yield the eye, Vance. Or we flay it from your skull while you watch your slum burn from below."

Silas’s left socket throbbed with a pain so intense it turned his peripheral vision into a violent kaleidoscope of silver and magenta. He felt the ancient core inside him reacting to the Inquisitor’s presence, violently thrumming against his cheekbone like a trapped bird beating its wings against iron bars. 

"Lyra," Silas whispered, his voice barely audible over the roaring wind whipped up by the giant gears below. "Can you bypass the wheel's primary valve if I buy you thirty seconds?"

"Thirty seconds?" She glanced at the vanguard’s null-shields, her perceptive eyes mapping the translucent blue threads of mana stringing between the soldiers and the vault walls. "If those null-shields hit us, I can't even ignite a match, let alone crack a high-celestial seal. Their aura is suffocating the ley lines."

"Then I'll break the shields," Silas gritted his teeth, shifting his stance. His heavy boots scraped against the frosted stone. "When I move, you run for the central axle."

"Silas, if you unseal the eye completely—"

"Now, Lyra!"

Silas reached up and tore the leather eye-patch from his face.

Light—blinding, unholy, and ancient—erupted from his left eye socket. It was not mere illumination; it was a physical force, a lance of dense, concentrated cosmic energy that tore through the ambient dark of the vault. Silas roared, a sound of unadulterated agony as the unstable astral core inside his skull flooded his nervous system with liquid starfire. The veins on the left side of his face and neck blackened, glowing with brilliant silver light beneath his skin.

The vanguard knights recoiled as the sheer atmospheric displacement hit them. Their null-shields sputtered, the ancient cosmic magic forcing the suppressive runes to overload and crack like cheap glass. 

Silas lunged forward, the weight of his broadsword lightened by the violent gravitational distortion surging around him. He brought the heavy silver blade down in a brutal, arc-like sweep. The edge slammed into the lead vanguard knight’s shield. The resulting shockwave tore through the walkway, shattering the obsidian floor tiles into a thousand flying shards and pitching two of the inquisitorial guards straight into the spinning bronze cogs below. Their screams were cut abruptly short by the sound of crushing steel and bone.

"Forward!" Malakor bellowed, raising his own broad-headed mace, which crackled with golden lightning. "Contain the core! Slay the girl!"

Lyra ducked beneath a sweeping halberd, her light frame granting her speed where the heavy-armored knights were clumsy. She sprinted toward the glowing glass cylinder at the center of the walkway—the valve housing that channeled Silas's magic into the gargantuan gear system. Her daggers twirled in her hands. She sliced through two exposed mana-lines on the housing, her eyes burning bright blue as she instantly decoded the ancient flow of the celestial runes.

"It's a mirror-lock!" Lyra screamed over the deafening mechanical roar. "Silas! The wheel isn't pulling your magic—it's reflecting it! It's using your eye to balance its own unstable orbit!"

Silas parried a strike from Malakor, the impact rattling the bones in his arms and forcing him back a step. Blood poured freely from his left eye down his chin, boiling off his chest-plate. His vision on his right side was normal, but his left side showed him the world in cold, geometric strands of raw energy. He could see the Inquisitor's beating heart, the flow of stolen mana in his golden armor, and worse—he could see the massive beam of destruction building beneath their feet, aiming straight up into the foundations of the lower slums.

"Then how do we stop it?" Silas barked, parrying another heavy blow, his silver blade leaving trails of ozone in the air.

"We don't stop it!" Lyra shouted, plunging her daggers deep into the crystal housing. Celestial sparks cascaded over her gloves, burning through the leather. "We overload the mirror! But Silas... if I invert the flow, the core in your head is going to try to pull the whole wheel back into you!"

"Do it!" Silas yelled.

"Silas, it'll kill you!"

"I said do it, Thorne!" 

Malakor stepped inside Silas's guard, slamming the heavy pommel of his mace against Silas's jaw. The disgraced knight stumbled back, his boots slipping on the blood-slicked, fracturing stone. Before he could regain his balance, Malakor’s armored boot caught him in the chest, sending Silas crashing onto his back right at the edge of the collapsing walkway.

The High Inquisitor loomed over him, raising his lightning-sheathed mace for a executing strike. "A noble death for a traitor, Vance. But your flesh is irrelevant. The core will survive the smash."

Behind Malakor, Lyra ripped her daggers backward, tearing a glowing web of celestial lines directly out of the control valve.

The giant purge wheel beneath them screeched—a sound like a dying god. The bronze gears locked violently. The immense kinetic energy built up within the miles-wide machine had nowhere to go. Pressure violently reversed. 

A column of pure, unrefined cosmic radiance blew out from the center of the wheel, shooting upward through the vault ceiling like a lance of divine judgment. The walkway cracked in two. 

Malakor lost his footing as the floor beneath him shattered into dust, pitching backward toward the abyss. Silas scrambled to grab the ledge, his gauntlets digging into the breaking stone, his left eye blazing with an unbearable, blinding intensity as the inverted ley-line feedback violently lashed back into his skull.

The floor beneath Lyra slid into the dark. She leaped, catching the edge of the stone platform inches from Silas's hand.

Above them, the ceiling caved in, stone and ancient ruins raining down into the void. Through the growing tear in the vault roof, Silas looked up through his bleeding, glowing eye—and saw the lower sectors of the Citadel already bathed in the rising, crackling beam of white-hot astral light. The purge had not been stopped; it had been redirected into the district's structural pillars.

And from the blinding light above, something vast, ancient, and shadowy began to descend into the rift.

episodes.content:
The air in the subterranean vault turned to liquid copper and ash. 

Silas Vance spat a mouthful of black dust onto the fractured flagstones, his fingers digging into the stone to hoist himself upright. His greaves groaned under his weight, the cold metal biting through the padded arming doublet beneath. Above him, the ceiling had ceased to be stone; it was a jagged throat torn open to the dark, through which a column of blinding, white-gold mana spewed violently skyward into the foundation pillars of the lower sector.

Every breath tasted of scorched ozone and ancient dust. 

"Silas!" Lyra’s voice was a jagged thread cut short by the thunder of grinding architecture. 

He turned his head slowly, muscles burning. Through the swirling haze of pulverised plaster and venting steam, he saw her. She was crouched beside the ruined housing of the flow-valve, her dual daggers struck deep into a hairline crack in the vault wall to keep her anchor against the atmospheric draft. The inverted mana pulse had created a localized vacuum—an unnatural pull dragging every scrap of debris toward the shattered center.

"I’m here," Silas grunted. He reached for the hilt of his broadsword, buried half a foot into a shattered paving stone. As his gauntleted hand wrapped around the leather grip, a fresh spasm of agony tore through the left side of his face. 

His corrupted eye—the shattered astral core sealed beneath his eye socket—was singing. Not a sound, but a vibration that vibrated through the bone of his jaw, echoing the high-pitched hum of the celestial clockwork dying around them. The violet light bleeding from beneath his eyelid cast long, distorted shadows across the chamber.

Ten paces away, movement broke through the dust. High Inquisitor Malakor pushed himself out of the rubble of his fallen null-shield platform. His ornate, silver-threaded robes were shredded, stained with dark grease and his own blood, but the silver mask covering his upper face remained unbroken. Behind the slits, Malakor’s eyes burned with a hysterical, fanatical rage.

"Heretics," Malakor rasped, his voice bubbling through a punctured lung. He raised his remaining hand, the gold-ringed fingers trembling as he tried to weave a suppression glyph in the air. "The purge wheel... you have untethered the Anchor..."

"Shut your mouth, Inquisitor," Silas growled, freeing his blade with a harsh metallic scrape. 

"You don't understand what was sleeping under the gears, Vance!" Malakor screamed, his voice rising above the deafening groan of the iron vault. "It wasn't a mechanism! It was a cage!"

A sudden, absolute drop in atmospheric pressure rendered the room instantly silent. The deafening roar of falling masonry vanished. The dust suspended in the air froze in place, locked in tiny, shimmering clusters. 

Frost flared across the broadside of Silas’s silver sword, crawling up his vambrace in jagged, white needles. The temperature plunged so fast that the blood smeared across Malakor’s mask crystallized into crimson ice.

Lyra gasped, a cloud of frozen vapor bursting from her lips. "Silas... look up."

Silas raised his gaze.

Descending through the pillar of raw, white-gold radiance was not a piece of machinery, nor a fragment of shattered sky. It was a silhouette of impossibly dense, geometric light—a creature forged from black iron ribs and burning, stellar marrow. It had no face, only a vertical slit of absolute void flanked by twin rings of turning, runic rings that clicked with mechanical precision.

A Null-Star Archon. An ancient entity from the First Conjunction, entombed by the High Council centuries ago to fuel the Citadel’s endless mana consumption.

The pressure returned in a physical wall of force. Silas was slammed down onto one knee, the flagstones beneath him spider-webbing under the sudden surge of artificial gravity. His left eye screamed—a sensation like liquid glass being poured directly into his brain. The corrupted core within him recognized the Archon. It was trying to synchronize.

"Lyra..." Silas squeezed his left eye shut, binding his hand tightly over his socket as blood mixed with glowing violet serum leaked between his gauntleted fingers. "The ley lines... can you see a breach?"

Lyra was flat against the wall, her knuckles white around her dagger hilts. Her natural gaze, normally sharp and calculated, was wide with terror. To her vision, the invisible currents of cosmic magic were no longer flowing; they were tearing apart like frayed ropes, whipping wildly through the air and disintegrating stone on contact.

"The whole vault is collapsing into a gravity well!" she yelled over the mounting hum, her voice tight with strain. "The structural pillars above us are buckling! If the Archon fully unfolds its rings, the pressure will flatten this entire sector into slag!"

"Malakor!" Silas barked, forcing himself back to his feet inch by painful inch. "Your Council built this damn cage! How do we lock it back down?"

Malakor did not answer. The High Inquisitor was kneeling on the floor, his head thrown back, his gloved hands reaching toward the descending entity in blind adoration. "The purity of the Void..." he whispered, his skin turning gray as the Archon sucked the raw heat from the room. "The Council promised... we would transcend..."

Before Malakor could finish his prayer, one of the Archon’s outer runic rings swept through the air. It moved without velocity, simply existing in one place and then another. The ring passed cleanly through Malakor's torso. There was no blood, no sound of tearing flesh. The Inquisitor simply unravelled—his flesh, armor, and bone turning into a fine drift of gray salt that was swept instantly into the central vacuum.

"Silas!" Lyra screamed.

The Archon lowered its central eye—the rift of absolute void—toward them.

A localized shockwave tore through the chamber. The floor broke into floating, jagged islands of stone. Silas lunged forward, his heavy boots launching him across a widening chasm. He grabbed Lyra by the collar of her leather tunic just as the flagstone she had been standing on disintegrated into fine sand beneath the Archon's passive aura.

He slammed her behind his armored bulk, driving his silver broadsword deep into a cracked foundation beam to anchor them both against the rising gravitational pull.

"Listen to me," Silas spat, his vision swimming with streaks of purple and gold. His left eye felt like it was expanding, threatening to split his skull open. "My core... it’s reacting to its heart. It’s drawing the entity’s focus."

"If you unseal that eye completely, it will burn your mind out, Silas!" Lyra grabbed his forearm, her daggers hanging by their leather lanyards from her wrists. "You can't channel that much raw cosmic mana without an Astral Catalyst!"

"I don't plan on channeling it," Silas snarled, his teeth stained red. He looked at her, his right eye clear, hardened by decades of war and regret, while his left flared with an unholy, crackling stellar light. "I'm going to overload it. The same way you inverted the valve."

"That's madness! If you force a feedback loop between your shattered core and a First-Age Archon, the resulting spatial fracture will—"

"It will tear a hole out of this vault," Silas interrupted, his voice dropping to a gravelly whisper as the Archon’s shadow fell over them. "Or it will bury us. Either way, we aren't dying in Malakor’s cage."

Above them, the Archon’s inner ring aligned with its central void. A sound like a thousand glass bells shattering at once echoed through the deep stone. The air turned so cold that Silas's breath froze in his throat. A needle-thin beam of black light began to coalesce at the entity's center, aimed directly at the foundation beam beneath their feet.

"Get behind my shield line!" Silas roared.

He let go of his broadsword's hilt and ripped off the leather eye-patch concealing his left socket.

The sudden release of corrupted cosmic essence was instant and blinding. A fountain of raw, violent violet flame erupted from Silas's eye, burning through the air and striking the Archon’s descending beam head-on. The collision did not create an explosion; it created an unnatural stillness, a pocket of inverted reality where light turned dark and stone dissolved into floating dust.

Silas screamed—a raw, tearing sound from the depths of his chest—as the feedback surged backward along the light beam, pouring straight back into his body. The runes carved along his silver broadsword began to glow red-hot, then white, then cracked under the impossible pressure.

"Lyra... now!" Silas choked out, his body convulsing as the cosmic power threatened to tear his physical form apart. "The structural flaw!"

Lyra jumped over his shoulder, her daggers burning with blue runic light as she identified the single, vibrating ley-line junction exposed by the collision of their powers. She drove both blades into the glowing crack in the foundation pillar with all the strength in her young frame.

The world shattered.

The pillar split end to end. The vast, subterranean vault lurched sideways as the upper foundations of the Astral Citadel gave way. Thousands of tons of stone, iron, and ancient clockwork collapsed downward, burying the Archon in a cascade of rubble, while a geyser of unleashed spatial energy blew the floor beneath Silas and Lyra into a falling vortex of darkness.

As Silas fell into the abyss, his sight fading to black, he heard the terrible, resonant screech of the Archon breaking free of its burial—and the sound of the Citadel above beginning its long, catastrophic descent.

They discover that the Citadel's magic is siphon-fed from an ancient, chained cosmic horror rather than the celestial heavens. As the spatial collapse severs the containment seals, the star-bronze gates shatter, releasing a primordial entity from the starless void beneath the world.

episodes.content:
The abyss did not simply receive them; it devoured them.

Wind howled through the subterranean shaft like a dying god’s breath, suffocating and hot with the stench of scorched silver and crushed granite. Silas slammed his left hand out, his gauntlet skidding along the slick basalt face of the plunging shaft. Sparks erupted in blinding blue arcs, screaming against the wet stone as the friction tore down to the bone of his wrist. With his right arm, he clamped Lyra tight against his heavy cuirass, taking the brunt of the cascading stone and shattered masonry raining from the vault above.

"Hold fast!" Silas rasped, his voice tearing in his throat. 

Below them, the darkness was absolute, save for the erratic, violet-white strobe leaking from his own left socket. His corrupted astral core surged inside his chest like a trapped viper, rattling against his ribs, fighting the heavy suppressive runes carved into his flesh. Every pulse flooded his vision with phantom constellations and blinding geometric fractures.

Lyra didn't scream. She pinned her head against the notch of his pauldrons, her fingers digging deep into the leather under-straps of his plate armor. Her breath came in sharp, rapid gasps against his collarbone. "Wall leaning twenty degrees left!" she shouted over the roar of the collapse. "Brace for impact!"

A jagged shelf of ancient star-glass jutted from the abyss wall like a broken tooth. Silas twisted in midair, hurling his body beneath hers.

They slammed into the projection. The force of the impact snapped Silas’s breath out of his lungs in a red mist. The star-glass shattered beneath his back, absorbing just enough momentum to turn a fatal drop into a bone-crunching tumble down a steep slope of wet, forgotten masonry. They hit the floor of the lower chamber violently, sliding across freezing, ankle-deep water before grinding to a halt against a monolithic pillar of black basalt.

For a long, agonizing minute, the world narrowed to the sound of falling rubble far above and the ragged, wet rattle of Silas’s lungs.

The air here was different. The atmospheric pressure pressed inward against their eardrums, dense with the metallic tang of unrefined celestial magic and the heavy, damp rot of centuries. It smelled of ozone, drowned stone, and ancient, unvented mana.

"Lyra..." Silas grunted, coughing until his teeth metallic-tasted of blood. He tried to push himself up, but his left arm collapsed under him, deadened by the backflow of his corrupted core.

A small, firm hand gripped his shoulder. Lyra was already on her knees beside him, her face pale beneath a smearing of soot and black brine. Her dual runic daggers were out, their faint silver edge-glow casting a soft, pale halo over her sharp features. 

"Don't move," she whispered, her gaze sweeping the gloom above them. Her breath misted in the sudden, bone-chilling drop in temperature. "The ceiling hasn't settled. If the upper Citadel’s keystones give way, three million tons of marble will bury us before we can take another breath."

"The Archon?" Silas demanded softly, forcing his eye open. 

The left eye flickered violently, its iris a swirling vortex of unstable nebula-purple that cast long, unnatural shadows against the surrounding ruins. Through that ruined lens, the world was a jagged web of leaking magic—bright indigo veins of raw ley power pulsing through the stone like severed arteries.

"Trapped above. Or buried beneath High Inquisitor Malakor's ashes," Lyra said, though her voice lacked conviction. She lowered herself to one knee, dipping two fingers into the stagnant black water pooling around their boots. She pulled her hand back immediately, wincing as tiny, luminescent needles of pale blue static danced across her skin. "This isn't ground water. It’s condensed celestial runoff. We’re miles beneath the Underbelly. We’ve fallen into the Citadel's Foundational Root."

Silas managed to sit up, leaning his heavy plate back against the carved basalt pillar. He dragged his heavy silver broadsword across his knees, the steel groaning as the ambient magical pressure in the room resonated with the runes etched into the blade's fullers. 

"The Root was sealed during the Mana Eclipse," Silas growled, his hand instinctively reaching up to touch the raised, blackened veins creeping up the side of his neck. The core inside him throbbed violently, responding to the ambient power of the chamber. "The High Council declared this sector dead. They capped the ley-conduits and let the lower districts rot above it."

"They didn't cap it," Lyra said softly. She stood, turning a slow circle, her gaze fixed on the ceiling and the towering structures emerging from the dark. "They hid it."

Silas pushed through the white-hot pain in his chest and forced himself to his feet. The weight of his armor felt doubled in the dense air. He looked around.

They were standing in an immense, forgotten nave. Monolithic pillars, thick as siege towers and carved from seamless void-stone, stretched up into an abyss of vaulted arches. But these pillars were not decorative; they were bound in massive chains of cold-forged star-bronze, each link etched with glowing, archaic glyphs that hummed with a low, bone-vibrating resonance. 

The sound was everywhere—a deep, rhythmic *thrum-thrum-thrum* that vibrated through the soles of their boots and resonated in their teeth. It sounded like the slow, labored heartbeat of a dying titan.

"Look at the runes, Silas," Lyra whispered, stepping closer to one of the massive chained pillars. She traced a finger an inch above the glowing metal, careful not to break the arc of blue static. "These aren't containment glyphs for an architecture. They’re siphon seals. Ancient First-Era script."

Silas squinted through his corrupted eye, the purple flare washing over the archaic text. "Read it."

"It says... *'Here lies the Engine of the Unbroken Starlight. Let the Blood of the First Arch-Mage feed the Spire, lest the void reclaim the sky.'*" Lyra turned back to him, her sharp eyes wide with a realization that made her blood run cold. "The Citadel’s magic... the infinite power the High Council boasts of... it was never drawn from the upper celestial heavens."

"It’s being pulled up from below," Silas finished, his voice dropping into a somber register. "From whatever is chained down here."

A sharp, explosive crack echoed through the chamber, followed by the deep screech of tearing metal. 

Both of them froze. 

Above them, where the ceiling vanished into the black, the falling debris had ceased, but a new light was beginning to bleed down through the rift they had fallen through. It wasn't the warm solar flare of the Citadel’s upper lanterns, nor the cold silver of starlight. It was a thick, viscous crimson—the sickly, suffocating light of a dying star bleed-out.

The spatial detonation from the floor above hadn't just collapsed the vault; it had severed the primary siphon conduits. 

"The pressure is shifting," Lyra said, her voice tight with rising panic. She pointed her dagger toward the center of the nave. The stagnant black water was beginning to ripple, pulled outward in concentric rings toward a massive, sunken dais at the far end of the hall. "The ley lines are reversing their flow. Silas, if those seals burst—"

"They’re already bursting," Silas said, stepping in front of her and lifting his broadsword. 

At the center of the sunken dais, four towering star-bronze gates, each fifty feet high and locked together by a massive central locking ring, began to glow with a blinding, white-hot intensity. The ancient runes etched along their surfaces weren't glowing with power—they were melting. Droplets of liquid bronze hissed violently as they hit the black water, sending up clouds of scalding, ozone-scented steam.

From behind the melting gates came a sound that sent a cold shudder straight down Silas’s spine. 

It wasn't the roar of a beast, nor the mechanical grinding of an ancient defense ward. It was a breath. A long, agonizingly slow inhalation that pulled the very air out of Silas's lungs, dragging the mist, the steam, and the blue static straight toward the hairline fractures spreading across the star-bronze doors.

Silas’s left eye burned with unbearable fury. Black blood trickled down his cheek from the socket as his corrupted core violently aligned its pulse with whatever lay behind that gate. He fell to one knee, clutching his head, a ragged groan escaping his lips as visions of shattered suns and endless obsidian voids flooded his consciousness.

"Silas!" Lyra dropped beside him, grasping his gauntlet. "Resist it! If your core syncs with that lock, it will draw you in!"

"It's... calling the fracture..." Silas gasped, his vision swimming in violent hues of indigo and scarlet. "The Archon... it wasn't the source... it was a scout..."

The central locking ring on the giant star-bronze gates gave a final, deafening sound like a thunderclap. 

The massive bronze chains wrapped around the chamber's pillars snapped one by one, whipping through the dark like iron serpents and smashing into the basalt walls. The towering gates did not swing open; they buckled inward, torn from their mountings by an immense, gravitational pull from the darkness beyond.

A blast of pure, unrefined cosmic pressure hit Silas and Lyra like a physical wall, throwing them back into the knee-deep brine.

Through the mist and the blinding storm of red sparks, Silas forced his head up. 

The gates were gone. In their place sat a tear in the fabric of the realm—a jagged, starless void that did not reflect light, bounded only by floating, shattered glyphs of an ancient civilization. And from the depths of that starless dark, a massive, luminescent hand—woven from threads of dying white fire and ancient, calcified mana—slowly reached out, its fingers locking onto the edge of the broken threshold.

Lyra scrambled back, her daggers raised, her breath catching in her chest. "Silas... what is that?"

Silas dragged himself up, his broadsword trembling in his grip, his corrupted eye blazing like a dying star. 

"The Citadel’s true foundation," Silas whispered, his cynical voice heavy with utter dread. "And we just broke its leash."

episodes.content:
The star-bronze gates did not simply break; they unraveled. 

Massive, golden-hued splinters measuring the length of siege towers sheared off the hinges, ricocheting through the cavernous gloom of the Foundational Root. One jagged beam slammed into the petrified trunk beside Sir Silas Vance, missing his shoulder by inches. The kinetic impact hit like a thunderclap, forcing air from his lungs and sending a wave of crushed stone and dry rot washing over his heavy plate armor. 

Then came the cold. 

It was not the crisp, clean bite of a winter high in the outer realms. It was an absolute, weightless void-chill—the temperature of dead space where stars had long since burned out. The moisture on Silas’s iron gorget froze instantly into a milky crust of frost. Beside him, Lyra Thorne gasped, her breath blooming into a dense plume of white before collapsing into tiny, floating ice crystals.

"Silas!" she shouted, her voice thin, stripped of resonance by the plummeting atmospheric pressure. 

Silas didn't answer. He couldn't. 

His left eye—the socket scarred by the ancient cosmic ritual that had ruined his knightly standing—was burning. The unstable void-essence trapped within the tissue throbbed in direct, sickening unison with the darkness pouring through the shattered doorway. White-hot agony flared behind his brow, casting his vision into dual realities: with his right eye, he saw the crumbling, root-choked vault; with his left, he saw the universe torn open, bleed-lines of raw, sickly violet mana pouring like infected blood from a jagged tear in the cosmos.

"Get behind the pillar!" Silas choked out, his hand flying to the hilt of his heavy silver broadsword. The silver woke with a faint, trembling amber hum, its carved solar runes flaring to life as he drew the long blade from its scabbard. The light was small, frail, a ember cast against a hungry sea.

Out from the shattered bronze frame spilled the primordial entity. 

It possessed no singular shape. It was a shifting, non-Euclidean silhouette of anti-light, a mass of swirling, starless silence that absorbed the ambient glow of the citadel’s dying ley lines. Tendrils of heavy, gravity-warping mist spilled across the wet stone floor, dissolving the petrified wood of the roots into fine grey ash upon contact. Where it touched the air, sound died.

"The ley lines..." Lyra scrambled back against a heap of carved masonry, her dual runic daggers drawn, though her hands trembled. Her gaze was locked upward, her rare sight tracing the glowing veins of celestial magic that wove through the vault's vaulted ceiling. "Silas, look at the vault arch! The Citadel isn't drawing power from the star-wells above. The High Council built the whole damn city as a harness!"

Silas narrowed his good right eye, shifting his posture into a low, defensive stance. The weight of his armor, usually a comforting anchor, felt agonizingly heavy against the crushing gravity bleeding off the void-creature. "A harness?"

"A siphon," Lyra corrected, her sharp tongue edged with pure terror. "They didn't chain this thing to keep the realm safe. They anchored the Astral Citadel directly into its throat. The magic that lights the upper spires, the energy that powers the Council's wards—it’s all purified void-rot, distilled through those bronze gates! And now that the seals are gone..."

She didn't need to finish the thought. 

Above them, deep within the dark belly of the stone ceiling, a low, tectonic groan echoed down. The foundation of the Astral Citadel was cracking. Without the star-bronze gates to act as a dam, the cosmic entity was expanding, seeking the light, pushing upward into the very stone that supported the gilded plazas, the high towers, and the starving slums beneath them.

The entity shifted. A pale, luminary eye—larger than a war galley, filled with spiraling galaxies of decaying color—unfolded within the heart of the darkness. It fixed its gaze upon Silas.

Or more precisely, upon Silas’s left eye.

*Kinsman.*

The sound wasn't spoken. It was a violent physical pressure that detonated inside Silas's mind, driving him to one knee. Stone shattered beneath his armored kneepad. His silver broadsword struck the floor, sparks spraying into the frost. He clamped a gauntleted hand over his face, but violet light erupted between his fingers, scorching the leather under-glove.

"Silas!" Lyra darted forward, her short, nimble boots slipping slightly on the frost-dusted flags. She seized his shoulder, trying to drag him back. "We have to fall back toward the lower aqueducts! If we stay in this chamber when the central root collapses—"

"It knows me," Silas rasped through gritted teeth, his breath rattling in his throat. Blood, dark and shimmering with faint purple flecks, began to drip from his left nostril. "The core... the core the Arch-Mage thrust into my skull... it was a fragment of this thing."

Lyra’s eyes widened. She glanced from Silas’s agonizingly bright socket to the colossal horror looming over the shattered gateway. "Thai didn't try to save you during the Eclipse," she whispered, the realization striking her like a blade. "He used you as a vessel. A mobile lock."

"I was... the emergency key," Silas spat, forcing himself back to his feet inch by agonizing inch. The amber solar runes on his broadsword flickered wildly, struggling against the overwhelming pressure of the void. "If the gates ever fell... the Council's fail-safe was never a spell. It was a sacrifice."

The primordial entity extended a single, sweeping limb—a massive arc of pressurized darkness edged with crystalline fragments of broken stars. It moved without velocity, simply ceasing to be in one location and appearing in another. The displacement created an atmospheric shockwave that blasted the remaining wooden roots to splinters.

"Move!" Silas roared.

He lunged forward, thrusting Lyra violently behind him into the recess of a fallen archway. He raised his silver broadsword with both hands, channeling every shred of his remaining solar magic into the blade. The silver flared into a brilliant, blinding orange sun-fire, casting long, frantic shadows against the vault walls.

The entity’s limb collided with the sun-fire.

The sound was like glass breaking under a blacksmith's hammer. Silas’s boots skidded backward across the flagstones, carving deep furrows into the ancient masonry. The force vibrated up his arms, cracking his steel pauldrons and popping the rivets from his right breastplate. The solar fire on his blade whined, turning purple at the edges as the void began to consume his magic.

"Lyra!" Silas spat blood onto his visor. "The conduit behind the root-pillar! Can you realign the ley-flux?"

Lyra was already moving, her eyes blazing with the strange, pale light of her stargazer sight. She scrambled up a pile of ruined masonry toward a massive, cylindrical stone pillar embedded with rows of ancient celestial runes. Her fingers flew over the carved surfaces, her runic daggers slicing into her own palms to coat the stone in living blood—a raw catalyst to force the magical lines to connect.

"The runes are dead, Silas!" she screamed back over the howling spatial wind. "The High Council drained the conduit dry centuries ago! There's no celestial mana left in the stone to jump-start the seal!"

"Then find another source!" 

The void entity pressed harder. Silas’s knees buckled. The silver broadsword was hair-line cracked now, purple veins spreading across the forged metal like a spiderweb. His left eye was burning so fiercely he could feel his optical nerve charring inside his skull. The entity was pulling him—not physically, but pulling his very soul, drawing the shattered fragment of its core back into its massive, terrifying whole.

*Return,* the voice thundered inside his head, cold and devoid of malice, carrying only the terrifying indifference of an ocean drowning a moth. *The false sky must fall.*

"Lyra!" Silas barked, his vision fading to absolute violet. "Now!"

"I can redirect the line!" Lyra shouted from the top of the conduit pillar. She stood bathed in the sickly glow of the entity, her dark hair whipped wildly by the localized gravity storms. "But I have to route the flow through *you*! Your eye is the only power source left in this pit!"

Silas let out a harsh, broken laugh that turned into a cough of blood. "Do it, girl! Before I turn into one of those damn things!"

Lyra plunged both of her bloodied runic daggers directly into the primary conduit node atop the pillar. 

Instantly, a beam of blinding, uncorrupted stellar light erupted from the stone, violently connecting to the glowing socket of Silas's left eye. The pain was beyond anything he had endured on the battlefields of the Mana Eclipse. Silas screamed—a raw, guttural sound that echoed through the dying depths of the Foundational Root—as his body became the living bridge between the cosmic horror and the ancient containment grid.

The air around them inverted. The gravity collapsed inward. 

The void entity shrieked—a sound that shattered every remaining piece of star-bronze in the vault. But instead of being driven back into the rift, the entity violently bound itself to Silas's neural link. The ley lines spun wildly out of control, turning from violet to a volatile, blinding white.

Above them, the ceiling gave way. 

A massive section of the Citadel's upper foundations—a two-hundred-foot spire of solid marble and gilded iron—shattered and began its catastrophic descent directly into the chamber, bringing down the sky upon them both.

As an Inquisitor strikes and a colossal void horror opens its gaze beneath the dissolving floor, the upper structures crumble down upon them, leaving Silas struggling to maintain control over his eye's corrupted mana.

episodes.content:
Dust tasted like sulfur and powdered bone.

Sir Silas Vance spat crimson onto the fractured marble, his right vision blurred by gray grit, his left eye burning with an agony that felt less like pain and more like a dying star attempting to burst through the lining of his skull. The blinding feedback loop from the ruined conduit had severed something deep within the ancient chamber's architecture, but the cost was etched straight into his optic nerve. Every jagged pulse of his heart sent a violent surge of violet, unstable light spilling across the fallen debris, casting long, jittering shadows against the broken vaults of the Astral Citadel’s underbelly.

"Lyra," he rasped, his voice low and scraping against his raw throat. The sound was immediately swallowed by the deep, grinding groan of thousands of tons of stone settling above them.

No answer came—only the wet, rhythmic thrum of the cosmic rift below, pulsing like a severed artery in the dark.

Silas pushed himself up, the thick steel plating of his left pauldron screeching as it scraped against a massive slab of white masonry. The weight resting across his shoulder was crushing, but the residual cosmic mana flooding his veins gave his muscles a false, feverish strength. He shoved the stone aside, his gauntleted hand trembling as he reached for the hilt of his heavy broadsword. The silver blade, etched with the dormant sigils of his former knighthood, hummed in dissonant, frantic harmony with the erratic flares from his left eye.

Ten paces away, a beam of black-veined marble lay hoisted at an awkward angle against a collapsed archway. Beneath it, a pale hand clutching a hilt of runic steel twitched against the gray rubble.

"Lyra!" Silas stumbled forward, his boots crunching heavily on pulverized crystal. He dropped to one knee, jamming the tip of his silver broadsword beneath the stone slab to gain leverage. "Hold on. Don't move."

"I'm... not dead, Vance," her voice was a hoarse, coughing whisper from the shadows beneath the stone. "Though... I might prefer it if you don't drop that... pillar on my chest."

Silas gritted his teeth, shifting his body weight onto the hilt. The unstable essence in his left eye flared blindingly, a harsh purple wave washing over the shattered stone. A jolt of raw spatial force traveled down his arm, through the silver steel, and snapped the marble slab in two with a concussive, deafening *crack*.

Lyra wriggled free instantly, her body wracked by violent coughing spasms that left her cracked leather tunic dusted in fine white powder. Her skin was ghastly pale, but her eyes—sharp, golden, and laced with the shimmering, thin threads of ley-line sight—were wide with a cold terror as she looked past his shoulder.

"It didn't close," she said, her breath fogging instantly as the chamber's temperature plummeted toward absolute zero. "The seal didn't bind the entity. It shattered the anchor."

Silas turned slowly, his heavy wool cloak snapping in a sudden, razor-sharp draft that smelled of absolute nothingness.

Where the central conduit had stood moments ago, there was no longer a pedestal, nor an ancient rune-carved altar. There was only an abscess in reality—a jagged, raw tear three fathoms wide, spilling cold, suffocating darkness that smelled of frozen iron and ancient rot. Wisps of dark, starlit tendrils licked at the jagged edges of the pit, slowly digesting the falling marble as if the heavy stone were made of salt water.

"You routed the feedback loop through my eye," Silas said, his voice flat, dangerously quiet. He touched the edge of his cheekbone with his gauntlet; the flesh was raw, blackened, and humming with a faint electric hiss. "You said it would ground the siphoning."

"It *did* ground it," Lyra snapped, pushing herself to her feet with the help of her twin runic daggers. The faint blue light of her blades flickered weakly, struggling to maintain its form against the overwhelming void mana choking the air. "If I hadn't used your core as a lightning rod, that spatial wave would have turned us into red mist instantly. The Citadel's foundations were already rotting, Silas. The High Council wasn't just siphoning the void creature—they were inflating their entire floating paradise on a balloon of stolen cosmic pressure!"

A sharp, deafening sound—like the snapping of a massive iron cable—reverberated through the floorboards beneath their boots.

The atmospheric pressure dropped violently. Silas felt his ears pop, a sharp sting trailing down his neck as the thin air grew lighter, pulled violently toward the cavernous ceiling. High above, through the swirling cloud of white dust, a shaft of artificial, blinding golden light pierced the dark.

"Look," Lyra whispered, pointing up with a trembling dagger.

The falling debris had stopped raining down, suspended in mid-air by massive, glowing rings of gold and white holy magic. Above the dust layer, high up in the lower tiers of the Citadel, giant mechanical locks were grinding into place with rhythmic, thunderous thuds that shook the marrow of Silas's bones.

"They're isolating the district," Silas said, recognition hardening his voice into iron. "The *Aethel-Scourge* containment protocol."

"They aren't trying to fix the collapse," Lyra gasped, her golden eyes darting franticly across the faint, breaking ley lines that threaded through the air around them. "They’re cutting the underbelly free. They’re dropping the entire lower slum district into the void tear to plug the hole!"

"They won't sacrifice the whole sector," Silas growled, though the doubt tasted bitter in his mouth. "There are forty thousand souls living in the low vaults."

"To the High Executive, those forty thousand are just fuel they haven't burned yet," Lyra retorted, lunging forward to grab his leather arm-guard. Her fingers were trembling violently against his arm. "Silas, look at the ley flows! The gold lines—that’s Council mana. They are actively pumping holy incendiary energy into the ceiling struts to burn out the structural anchors! They're dropping the roof directly on top of us!"

As if answering her words, the golden rings hanging suspended in the dust flared with blinding, terrifying intensity. The heavy, oppressive scent of sanctified oil and scorched ozone filled the chamber, briefly overpowering the metallic stench of the void.

A harsh, amplified voice boomed down from the glowing aperture above, sounding like brass gears grinding over smooth velvet.

*"Heretic Vance. Scholar Thorne. By decree of the First Executive and the Grand Inquisitor, this lower sector has been designated as hyper-corrupted. Your souls are commended to the silence of the outer dark."*

The golden light condensed, coalescing into three distinct figures descending through the swirling dust cloud on floating platforms of spun radiance. They wore tall, polished steel helm-masks adorned with sharp golden sunbursts, and carried massive, two-handed glaives that hummed with heat so intense it turned the falling dust into blinding sparks before it even touched the steel.

Inquisitors of Aethelgard.

"They sent the Sun-Eaters," Silas muttered, shifting his grip on his broadsword. The silver metal rippled as the wild, unstable cosmic energy from his left eye flowed down his arm and into the crossguard. The etched runes burned a terrifying, unstable violet that hissed against the cold air. "They aren't here to contain the breach. They're here to clean up witnesses."

"We can't fight them and the void at the same time!" Lyra shouted over the rising roar of the void rift behind them. The floor beneath their boots cracked, a massive fissure spreading directly between them and the descending light platforms. "The ground is dissolving, Silas!"

The lead Inquisitor stepped off his floating platform, hovering two inches above the crumbling marble as if gravity were a mere suggestion to his holy armor. His face was entirely hidden behind a polished faceplate of gold leaf, reflecting the chaotic, violet glare of Silas’s corrupted eye.

"Sir Silas Vance," the Inquisitor’s voice echoed, cold and utterly devoid of humanity. "You were stripped of your cloak for cowardice during the Mana Eclipse. Now you linger like a plague-rat in the dark. Drop your blade and accept the solar purification."

"I was stripped of my cloak because I refused to purge starving districts for your precious mana reserves, Vane," Silas said, recognizing the precise, cold cadence of the voice despite the mask's mechanical distortion. "I see the Council hasn't changed its methods. Still burning down the house to kill a spider."

"The Citadel must endure," the Inquisitor replied softly. He raised his massive glaive. The long steel blade burst into a sheet of white-hot, holy flame that pushed back the freezing void-chill by fifty yards in a single instant. "The lower sectors are acceptable losses."

"Not to me," Silas growled.

Behind them, the void tear shrieked—a sound like torn silk played through a shattered cathedral bell. A thick tendril of absolute blackness, studded with tiny, dying stars, whipped up from the dark abyss, slamming directly into one of the secondary Inquisitor’s hovering support platforms. The golden light shattered like cheap glass, and the armored construct dissolved into fine gray ash in less than a heartbeat.

The lead Inquisitor didn't even flinch. He swept his blazing glaive down in a wide, sweeping arc of golden fire. "Purge."

"Lyra, behind me!" Silas roared.

He swept his heavy broadsword up to parry the incoming wave of holy fire. The kinetic impact slammed into his arms like a falling siege engine, forcing him down onto one knee as the marble cracked beneath his boots. The silver sword shrieked under the thermal shock, but the violet cosmic mana bleeding from his eye surged through his gauntlets, twisting the golden flames into a spiraling vortex of chaotic purple sparks that detonated outward.

The concussive shockwave blew the surrounding dust clear, revealing the horrifying truth of their situation.

The entire floor of the underbelly was no longer supported by stone or steel anchors. It was floating on a thin, spiderwebbing shell of compressed ley-energy directly over an endless ocean of cosmic night. And directly below them, swimming in that cold darkness, a massive, multifaceted eye—larger than a cathedral—slowly opened, fixing its endless, ancient gaze squarely on Silas.

Silas’s left eye throbbed violently in exact response, echoing the wet rhythm of the colossal entity below. His sight split wildly—he saw the Inquisitor leaping forward with raised glaive, he saw Lyra weaving a desperate sealing ward with her daggers, and he saw the entire lower city above them beginning its final, terminal descent into the abyss.

"Lyra!" Silas screamed, feeling his mind fraying at the edges as the cosmic corruption bled deeper into his brain tissue. "The eye—it's locking onto me!"

"Don't look into it!" she screamed back, her runic daggers tracing brilliant blue arcs in the freezing air. "Silas, if your focus slips, the spatial field collapses entirely!"

The lead Inquisitor descended, his flaming blade inches from Silas’s throat, just as the ceiling above gave way completely, dropping a hundred-ton block of gold-leafed masonry straight down into the fragile chamber.

episodes.content:
The world lost its weight.

Dust did not fall; it drifted sideways, caught in the violet-black gravitational pull beneath the broken floor. Silas Vance slammed his silver broadsword down into a hairline fracture in the stone, his gauntleted fingers locking around the pommel as the catwalk tipped twenty degrees into the abyss. Beneath him, through the spider-webbing cracks of the lower district, a colossal, pupil-less eye forged from starlight and absolute cold blinked in the deep shadow.

An Inquisitor—face masked in polished porcelain, pauldrons glowing with the stark white light of Aethelgard’s high solar seals—lunged across the tipping slab. The executioner’s halberd whistled through the vacuum left by the dropping atmospheric pressure. Silas parried instinctively, the impact sending a shudder up his arm that rattled his teeth. Runic sparks hissed off his blade, dying instantly in the void-tainted air.

"Containment takes precedence!" the Inquisitor barked, voice muffled by his alabaster visor. "The Underbelly is condemned by order of the High Council!"

"You're three minutes late to the execution!" Silas spat. He shifted his weight, his iron boots skittering across the smooth granite. His left eyelid twitched, trapped in an agonizing spasm. Behind the socket, the shattered astral core burned with a sickening violet radiance, pulsing in rhythm with the horror waking beneath them. The skin surrounding his cheekbone felt like hot lead poured beneath flesh.

"Silas!" Lyra’s voice cracked over the grinding roar of iron gears shearing apart fifty feet above. She was crouched on a jutting support beam, her dual daggers plunged handle-deep into the masonry to anchor herself. Her pale eyes were wide, glowing faintly with the mirror-refraction of active stargazing. "The decoupling protocol isn't just dropping the floor! They’re collapsing the spatial anchors! If those ley lines snap cleanly, the void will swallow this entire sector whole before we even hit the bottom!"

"Can you breach the manifold?" Silas parried another strike, his broadsword leaving a trail of dull silver arc in the shadow. He stepped inside the Inquisitor's reach, slamming his armored shoulder into the soldier's chest. The Inquisitor stumbled, his boots slipping on the rim of the widening void rift.

"I can't reach it!" Lyra shouted, her dark hair whipped upward by the rising draft of cold, dead mana. "The main conduit is shielded behind three layers of ward-steel! Unless you have enough raw strike-power to break a High Council seal, we’re about to be erased from the star-charts!"

Silas gritted his teeth. The skin around his left socket began to tear, tiny droplets of black, star-flecked blood floating upward into the air. The corrupted core within him screamed to be released—a wild, ravenous heat trying to crack his skull from the inside.

"Get behind the main strut!" Silas bellowed.

"Silas, no!" Lyra gasped, instantly recognizing the shift in the ambient pressure around him. "Your eye—if you vent that much core-mana without a dampener, the corruption will eat your arm!"

"Better my arm than the abyss!"

The second Inquisitor sprang from the upper ledge, halberd raised for a downward strike meant to cleave Silas through his worn breastplate.

Silas didn't raise his blade. He ripped his left hand away from his sword's grip and tore off the heavy leather blindfold that bound his eye.

The air died.

The ambient hum of the Citadel's ancient engines vanished, replaced by a deafening, localized vacuum. A beam of corrupted cosmic fire—a violet-gold spear of volatile, unrefined astral energy—erupted from his exposed eye.

The beam struck the falling Inquisitor mid-air. The solar armor shattered like frosted glass; the soldier didn't even scream before the kinetic force launched him backward into the gaping maw of the void horror below.

Silas roared, a sound torn from his throat by raw physical agony. He dragged his gaze upward, sweeping the beam across the ceiling structure. The violet flame carved through three-inch-thick ward-steel like parchment, igniting the dormant ley line nodes embedded within the support struts.

"Lyra! Now!"

Lyra didn't hesitate. Spotting the exposed, glowing fracture in the ley conduit where Silas's raw core-fire had stripped away the shielding, she leapt from her perch. She fell ten feet through free space, her right dagger extended. The runic blade caught the exposed mana-conduit, plunging straight into the heart of the Citadel’s decoupled energy flow.

The reaction was instantaneous.

Instead of a clean, controlled severance of the district, the ley line backfired. A blinding pulse of azure light exploded outward, clashing violently with the violet void-fire radiating from Silas. The shockwave ripped through the chamber, shattering the remaining catwalks and crushing the remaining Inquisitors under tons of dislodged masonry.

The gravity snap was brutal. Silas was slammed back-first onto the breaking slab, his vision flashing white as his left eye violently collapsed back into a dull, thrumming burn.

The entire lower district plummeted.

For three breathless seconds, there was only the rushing wind and the terrifying, silent expanse of the void horror stretching its tendrils upward toward them. The tear in space was opening wide, ready to digest the fallen debris.

Then, the overloaded ley line violently discharged.

A subterranean burst of ancient warp-mana snapped like a stretched rubber band, bending the spatial curvature beneath the falling platform. The air folded in on itself with a sound like thunder striking an anvil.

Space twisted. The yawning mouth of the void horror was violently pinched shut by the emergency spatial folding, and Silas, Lyra, and hundreds of tons of rubble were redirected—hurled sideways through a tearing seam in the Citadel’s foundation walls.

Silas hit stone. Hard.

The impact drove every drop of air from his lungs. Armor plates groaned under the shock; his silver broadsword clattered across dark, ancient flags, coming to a halt against a high stone plinth.

Silas lay there, gasping, coughing up a metallic smear of dark blood. His left eye was blind now, completely dead to light, radiating an icy numbness that crept down his neck.

"Lyra..." he rasped, his voice barely a whisper against the suffocating silence of the new chamber.

"I'm... here," a voice groaned from a pile of collapsed granite ten yards away. Lyra hauled herself up, her left sleeve shredded, her forearm bruised purple, but her hands still tightly clutching her runic daggers. "Tell me we didn't land in the Void."

Silas forced himself up onto one elbow, his right eye adjusting to the deep, oppressive darkness.

This was not the Void. Nor was it the Underbelly.

The air was cold, but it carried no scent of ash or ozone. It smelled of ancient dust, dried embalming oils, and something intensely, terribly old.

Above them, far out of reach, the jagged hole they had crashed through was sealing itself—not through Council magic, but through massive, autonomous stone slabs sliding shut with a heavy, final *thud*.

Lyra struck a spark with her dagger against the floor. A small, pale-blue flame ignited on the blade’s tip, illuminating their immediate surroundings.

Silas froze.

They were standing in a vast, vaulted catacomb buried far deeper than any map of Aethelgard indicated. Lining the walls were not the pristine statues of the current High Council, but towering, armless monoliths carved from black star-stone—the forbidden architecture of the First Builders.

In the center of the hall sat a massive sarcophagus of crystalized solar glass.

Inside it was not a skeleton, nor a corpse.

Suspended in stasis was a man wearing the ancient, forgotten crest of the Solar Knights—the very same crest that had been stripped from Silas's own chest twenty years ago. But what made Silas's breath catch in his throat was the man’s face.

It was Arch-Mage Thai.

The man Silas had watched die during the Mana Eclipse. The man whose death had signed Silas’s dishonorable discharge.

And floating directly above the stasis tomb was a floating, orb-like seal—pulsing with the exact same corrupted, violet-gold cosmic essence that was presently burning a hole through Silas's own skull.

"Silas..." Lyra breathed, her dagger flame trembling as she stepped backward. "That's... that's not possible. Thai was cremated in the High Court."

Before Silas could answer, the silver broadsword lying near the plinth began to hum. The dark star-stone monoliths around the room flared to life, their ancient runes burning with a pale, unholy brilliance.

From within the crystal sarcophagus, Arch-Mage Thai’s eyes snapped open.

And they were glowing with the absolute, endless darkness of the void.
